C-GRACE4-GOVERNANCE.Summary: Make GRACE 4 the mandatory contract-first branch, database and merge governance layer for kafedra-planner.
C-GRACE4-GOVERNANCE.Problem: Development already has project-specific Codex roles and broad CI, but main is unprotected and there is no machine-enforced link between an approved change contract, its observed write scope, append-only database migrations, final verification, and merge eligibility.

Goals.Goal: Require significant implementation work to use one approved active C-* spec and plan on a short branch created from an exact main revision.
Fail closed when observed repository writes escape the approved GraceChangePlan scope.

Protect SQLite consistency with immutable applied migrations, contiguous append-only migration numbering, clean-install and base-to-head upgrade checks, integrity checks, pre-migration backup verification and restore evidence.
Expose deterministic GitHub checks for GRACE contract, database upgrade and final merge eligibility while preserving the existing project and release CI.
Integrate kafedra-* specialist roles inside GRACE tasks rather than replacing them.

Constraints.Constraint: GRACE CLI 4.0.5 and Bun 1.3.14 are engineering/CI tools only and must not become application runtime or offline-bundle dependencies.
No application feature or application schema migration is introduced by this governance change.
Existing AGENTS.md, architecture, release gates and repository-local Codex skills remain authoritative and are extended rather than replaced.
A merge is eligible only for an unchanged PR head with all configured mandatory checks successful; pending, failed, cancelled or unexpected skipped evidence is not acceptable.

GitHub server-side main protection is a repository administrative control; because the connected GitHub action surface cannot mutate branch protection, the repository must contain an idempotent desired-state script and documentation for applying it with an administrative token.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Introduce gRPC transport, a network service, Docker, cloud infrastructure or a production GRACE dependency.
Change current department-planning behavior, user data, database schema version or release version.
Merge unrelated open feature or release branches.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: GRACE 4 context, graph, verification and change artifacts validate with the pinned GRACE CLI.
A governed diff without exactly one approved active C-* bundle fails, and any write outside ObservedWriteScope fails.
An existing migration cannot be changed, renamed or deleted relative to the PR base.
A new migration is accepted only as the next contiguous NNN migration with migration regression coverage and M-DATABASE/V-M-DATABASE scope.
The database gate proves clean HEAD migration and exact-base-to-HEAD upgrade with quick_check and foreign_key_check; schema upgrades additionally prove a verifiable restorable pre-migration backup.
GitHub Actions runs GRACE checks on development branches, pull requests and main; GRACE / merge-gate succeeds only when contract and database jobs succeed.

The documented main protection contract requires pull requests, strict up-to-date status checks, squash-only merges, no force-push/delete, conversation resolution and all mandatory existing CI/release plus GRACE merge gates.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: GRACE final lint, governance regression tests, database upgrade/restore evidence and GitHub required checks are successful for one unchanged head SHA.

Assumptions.Assumption: main remains the canonical integration branch.
SQLite schema_migrations remains the authoritative ordered migration ledger.
GitHub administrators can apply the committed protection script once using gh with an administrative token.
